prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Phoenix to fix my air conditioning?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” HVAC company for everyone — the right choice depends on where in Phoenix you are, what’s wrong with the system, how fast you need service, and your budget. I can help you pick a great local contractor. Quick questions first:
- What’s your ZIP code or neighborhood?
- What symptom do you have (won’t turn on, blowing warm air, short-cycling, odd noise, leak)?
- Brand and age of the AC (if you know)?
- Do you need same‑day emergency service?

If you want to choose a good contractor yourself, use this checklist and process:

What to check
- Licensed in Arizona (search Arizona Registrar of Contractors for their ROC number).
- Insurance (general liability + workers’ comp).
- NATE-certified technicians or equivalent training.
- Good recent reviews on Google/Yelp/Angi/BBB (look at recent jobs, not just overall score).
- Clear written estimate (parts, labor, taxes, permit costs) and scope of work.
- Labor and parts warranty (ask length and what’s covered).
- Flat-rate pricing for diagnostics/repairs or clear time-and-materials policy.
- Experience with your brand of equipment (manufacturer dealer if it’s under warranty).

Questions to ask on the phone
- “Are you licensed/insured? What’s your ROC number?”
- “Do you charge a diagnostic fee? If so, is it credited toward repair?”
- “Do you have NATE-certified technicians?”
- “What warranty do you offer on parts and labor?”
- “If the unit needs a replacement, will you pull permits and provide an itemized quote?”

Red flags
- High-pressure “replace now” without proper diagnosis.
- Very low estimate compared with others (could be bait-and-switch).
- No license number or unwillingness to provide proof of insurance.
- Technician won’t show ID or provide a written estimate.

Ballpark repair costs (very approximate; will vary by Phoenix market)
- Capacitor or contactor: $100–$400
- Fan motor: $300–$800
- Compressor replacement: $900–$3,000+
- Refrigerant recharge (if allowed/available): $100–$400 (or much more if leak repair required)
- New central AC installation: $3,500–$12,000+ depending on size and efficiency

If you want, I can:
- Suggest 3–5 companies to call based on your ZIP code (I’ll tell you what to look for in their reviews and give a short script to call them).
- Draft a message/email you can send to companies asking for quotes.
Tell me your ZIP code and the symptoms and I’ll tailor recommendations.
